newsitem.title: UK: Budget offers UK property market little - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Budget offers UK property market little - analysts.

text.p: The UK budget did not bring any unpleasant surprises for the commercial property market but the Chancellor Kenneth Clarke failed to unveil any uplifting measures for the sector, property analysts said on Tuesday.

"The good news is there is nothing to rock and upset the commercial property market. But nothing has come through for commercial occupiers," Angus McIntosh, director of research at property consultants Richard Ellis, told Reuters.
Analysts said the market had been hoping for clarification on the rules relating to commercial property rates, the local taxes charged on property.
These currently allow the rates on adjoining properties to vary significantly, analysts said.

"The Chancellor...gives no indication that the government intends to sort out this mess. Tax payable by occupiers in older buildings can be two or three times higher than the tax on new buildings," McIntosh added.

The budget did include a move to close a "loophole" by which companies in the banking and insurance sectors can avoid paying VAT (Value-Added Tax) on the property they use for business purposes also received a lukewarm welcome from some.
The UK's Customs and Excise said this measure would increase revenue by 110 million stg in the first full year.
